To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present an analog measurement setup that improves the quality of EM traces of cryptographic RFID devices and that we show that commercial contactless smartcards, e.g., the Mifare DESfire MF3ICD4, are susceptible to SCA.
We present an analog demodu-lation technique for the SCA of cryptographic RFIDs that is easy to implement and improves the quality of the measurements compared to previously proposed methods.
the proposed analog demodulator is able to improve EM measurements and, consequently, to increase the success rate of SCA of cryptographic RFIDs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the security of cryptographic contactless smartcards, which is of high importance in a time where RFID devices are widely used in everyday life.
the development of new SCA techniques and the evaluation of their effectiveness.
the practical security of contactless smartcard implementations and provides a detailed evaluation of their resistance against SCA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the security of RFID devices is still far from being satisfactory.
the security of the Mifare DESfire MF3ICD 40 contactless smartcards can not be guaranteed in the presence of a powerful adversary.
the use of cryptographic RFIDs in sensitive applications is not secure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an analog demodulation system that allows us to extract secret information from cryptographic RFID tags with a higher accuracy and lower cost than previously possible.
the security of contactless smartcard systems has to be re-evaluated in the light of SCA.

the security of cryptographic RFID systems can be improved by applying a combination of cryptographic techniques (such as AES) and physical measures (such as the proposed analog demodulator) in order to protect them from side-channel analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SCA is a serious threat that has to be considered in the security analysis of contactless smart cards and RFID systems.
the SCA of RFIDs is a realistic threat and that it should be addressed in the future.
the security of cryptographic RFIDs can be significantly improved by employing a more robust and efficient cryptographic core, such as the AES.
